mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact the S&P 500 over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate suggests improving labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE drops below 6% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When both industrial production and employment increase, it signals strong economic activity, boosting S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Both INDPRO and PAYEMS increase but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates may lead to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 5 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS exceeds 1% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts increase but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in retail sales signals increased consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Retail sales increase but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPI) rises and federal funds rates are high, it may indicate tightening monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
regime_hint: high inflation and high interest rates
failure_condition: Both CPI and FEDFUNDS increase but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, low unemployment and high employment suggest economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Both UNRATE is low and PAYEMS is high but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.
